svg.aria-label: Who owns what: a matrix of six cross-cutting rules against the four live rows of the W5 set — the exploration FIX-1467, the held child epic FIX-1455, and two unfiled rows, the devtool view and a basic DevForce. ER-1, a non-human seat owns the task and the person answers through a flow action carrying the request's own principal, is decided and built by FIX-1455 and consumed by both unfiled rows. ER-2, Waiting-on-you is parked and Idle is runtime, is decided by FIX-1455 and consumed by the devtool view, which renders it, and by DevForce. ER-3, the reference runs and its hired team survives a redeploy, is built by FIX-1455 and consumed by DevForce. ER-4, every proving surface composes and adds no layer, is built by FIX-1455 and is conditional on the other two rows being filed, drawn as dashed cells reading BUILDS IF FILED. ER-18, the downstream-blocking walls, is decided by FIX-1467 and consumed by FIX-1455, which teaches the convention. ER-19, the done condition, is split across three legs: leg a, the reference app, is owned by FIX-1455; leg b, the live view, and leg c, the real configuration, each fall in an unfiled column and are drawn as empty dashed cells reading NO CHILD. Those two empty cells are the finding — the done condition is owned in one third, and an empty cell here means no child produces this, which is different from a blank cell meaning the row does not touch the rule. A note records that the canceled FIX-1458 no longer has a column, and that ER-1 and ER-2, which it used to own, moved to FIX-1455 while ER-18's walls were retargeted to FIX-1467. Seventeen further rules sit outside this matrix because they bind every row equally and need no column: eleven prohibitions, ER-5 to ER-14 and ER-22; four rules for how the set is run, ER-15 to ER-17 and ER-23; and two more proof rules, ER-20 and ER-21.
svg.text: WHO OWNS WHAT — TWO OF THE DONE CONDITION’S THREE LEGS HAVE NO CHILD

g.text: ER-1 · a non-human seat owns the task
ER-3 · the reference runs, and comes back
ER-4 · every surface composes, adds no layer
ER-19 · the done condition · three legs
the one committed owner — decides or builds it
consumes it, and must not re-decide it — not a wait
conditional — applies once that row is filed
NO CHILD — nothing in the set produces this
A blank cell is different: it means the row does not touch that rule.
The two empty cells are the finding: ER-19 names three artifacts and one has a producer. Until both gaps are filed, W5 cannot reach its own done condition.
FIX-1458 was canceled Sep 20 and no longer has a column. ER-1 and ER-2 moved to FIX-1455; ER-18’s walls were retargeted to FIX-1467. Neither was left ownerless.
Seventeen further rules bind every row equally and need no column: eleven prohibitions ER-5–14 + ER-22, four run-the-set ER-15–17 + ER-23, two proofs ER-20/21.
The set is open (ER-23) — a child filed later gets a column here and inherits every rule.
